To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sulfonamide-based compounds have a great potential to be used as MMP inhibitors, but the design of such compounds is not an easy task and requires a thorough knowledge about their structural features.
the MMP inhibitions are mainly controlled by the hydrophobicity of the molecules, and the presence of the hydrophilic groups such as -COOH and -OH in the molecule increases its inhibitions.

the study of the quantitative structure-activity relationships of 28 sulfonamide-based matrix metalloproteinase inhibitors, which were selected from the literature.
the synthesis of novel sulfonamides as MMP inhibitors and their biological evaluation.

the presence of a hydroxyl group at 3'-position of the phenyl ring, and a hydrogen bond acceptor at 5'-position of the same ring, and a 3,5-disubstituted phenyl group at 4'-position of the sulfonamide ring are the most important structural features to be considered for the development of highly active sulfonamide-based compounds.
the presence of a hydrophobic moiety in the sulfonamides enhances the MMP inhibition activity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a number of QSARs have been reported on sulfonamides as MMP inhibitors, but the results of these studies are not conclusive and consistent.
all the QSARs reported so far on sulfonamide derivatives are based on the same molecular descriptors, and the same descriptors are used to develop different models.
the sulfonamide-based inhibitors have been studied using a wide variety of QSAR methods and different molecular descriptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different ways to design potent MMP inhibitors, and there is a need for further research in this field to find more potent MMP inhibitors for the treatment of a variety of diseases.
the sulfonamide-based inhibitors can be further improved by incorporating the structural features that have been identified as the key factors for their MMP inhibitory activity.
